The U.S. Air Force has moved forward with production of two unmanned fighter aircraft under its Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program, rather than selecting a single design.
Contracts have gone to General Atomics for the FQ-42A Dark Merlin and Anduril for the FQ-44A Fury. Both platforms had previously been tested under the YFQ-42A and YFQ-44A designations.
The aircraft are intended to act as semi-autonomous wingmen alongside crewed fighters, helping increase combat mass without requiring a proportional rise in the number of pilots or traditional jets.
The approach is meant to spread risk and divide roles across multiple systems instead of relying on a single type of aircraft.
Rather than one universal unmanned combat aerial vehicle (UCAV), the Air Force is effectively building a mixed fleet, with each design offering different strengths that can be developed further over time.
In the near term, the goal is to field more than 150 of these combat-capable wingmen by the end of the decade, with early units used mainly for testing, validation, and gradual operational integration.
